leads.summary: A j1 response that arrives between four and ten seconds leaves the CLI and weather notification unavailable while the panel can still display it
leads.consequence: On automatic detection with no stored name, the changed no-argument helper now fetches the full j1 response under the old four-second %l timeout. If j1 completes after four seconds but before ten, the panel's forecast fetch succeeds while the CLI prints nothing (exit 1), the right-click notification says Weather unavailable, and the optional post-boot weather hook does not send a notification. This is conditional on latency and was not measured against the live service.
leads.triage: dropped; unmeasured latency; old %l also used 4 s; Opus rated negligible (final.md H2)

leads.summary: A syntactically valid j1 forecast without nearest_area loses the auto-detected CLI and notification entirely
leads.consequence: When wttr.in returns valid current_condition/weather data but omits nearest_area or areaName[0].value, the panel can show conditions but has no location label. The CLI exits 1 with no location and weather-status returns Weather unavailable; the previous head could instead show its separate %l location if that endpoint worked. Both shipped GUI smoke curl fixtures already model a j1 payload with current_condition but no nearest_area. Upstream's j1 renderer passes the weather-provider response through without adding nearest_area, so this field is not validated by the renderer. The prevalence of such responses in production is unknown.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus followup-1; confirmed conditional (source does not guarantee field; public service returned it); published only as a contingency within R1 suggested change

leads.summary: Existing GUI smoke fixtures do not supply the j1 field the new weather label needs
leads.consequence: Both fake curl implementations return current_condition but omit nearest_area for j1; after this change, neither can exercise the automatic-mode label even when the weather is displayed. Add nearest_area with areaName[0].value (and latitude/longitude if the intended fallback forecast is exercised) at the j1 printf in both files. The new weather-test.sh CLI stub has nearest_area but no current_condition and therefore does not exercise a combined label-plus-conditions payload.
leads.triage: dropped; factual but test-fixture coverage of unrelated smoke tests; low value for public comment

leads.summary: Open weather-location fix PRs ship plain-text curl fixtures incompatible with this PR's new j1 parser
leads.location: bin/omarchy-weather-location:23; test/shell.d/weather-test.sh:205-217; related open PRs #9977, #12138 and #12155
leads.consequence: Each of #9977, #12138 and #12155 changes the old %l line and adds a curl stub returning strings such as 'Copenhagen, Denmark' or '48.855800,2.349400' (or 'Paris, France'). If a merge carries those tests forward with this PR's j1 CLI, jq rejects those plain-text outputs; their expected auto-location assertions fail. Resolve their overlap by reconciling both implementation and fixtures rather than blindly concatenating tests. #12967 additionally asserts the removed %l fallback and its own alternative resolver, so its panel tests conflict with this PR's resolver unless intentionally reconciled.
leads.triage: factual, verified via intake/related/*-files.json; published as Related open PRs note (overlap only; test-incompatibility detail omitted)

leads.summary: Related fetch-bounds PR #12952 retains a locationProc that this PR removes
leads.consequence: #12952 adds locationRunSeq/locationProcExit/locationOutput and applyLocation(), and its applyLocation assigns root.wttrLocation; this head deletes the property, process and refresh launch. The same locationProc block is also changed by #12952. If combining the patches preserves those additions but not the old property and launch, it leaves unused state and writes an undeclared QML property on any invocation; if someone restores its launch to satisfy the other patch, it makes an extra obsolete %l request. The overlapping edits need an explicit resolution, not a mechanical carry-over. No claim that the unmerged head currently has this failure.
leads.triage: factual, verified via intake/related/12952-files.json; published in Related open PRs note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13097#issuecomment-5825735442) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13097#issuecomment-5833495669), checked at `e72888de`.

**Outcome:** both earlier findings are resolved. One smaller issue remains in the right-click notification (below).

| Earlier finding | Status at `e72888de` |
|---|---|
| CLI and right-click status name the `%l` location | **Resolved** for the place name. The notification's numbers still come from a separate lookup (new finding below) |
| Optional test improvement | **Resolved** |

**Verified:**
- With no `weather.json`, `omarchy weather location` now reads `nearest_area[0].areaName[0].value` from a location-less `https://wttr.in/?format=j1` request. That is the same URL the panel fetches (`Panel.qml:335`) and the same field its label uses. The CLI and the panel now name the same place, so the manual's advice to run the command "to see where it thinks you are" matches the panel again.
- The right-click notification (`omarchy-weather-status`) takes its place name from that command, so it now shows the panel's name too.
- `Model.reportLocationName` is tested with fixtures shaped like #12904: `Orient` with no configured name, `Tel Aviv` with one, and empty without a `nearest_area`.
- The stubbed-curl CLI case checks the output as well as the request format.
- `weather-test.sh` passes on the head. The new Model assertions fail on the previous head and base because the helper is missing. Run alone, the CLI case fails there because the old command prints the raw stub response.
- Failed or malformed wttr.in responses now give no CLI output (exit 1). Before, the command passed any non-empty successful body through as the place name, cut at its first comma.

**Label scope:** the earlier note about auto-detect users now covers more surfaces. `omarchy weather location` and the right-click notification show the `nearest_area` name too, not the IP-lookup city. That is consistent with the panel label #12904 asks for.

### Right-click notification looks up the weather again by bare name

`omarchy-weather-status` prints the panel's place name, but it still makes a second request for temperature and wind by that name alone (`bin/omarchy-weather-status:12-13`):

```text
Stubbed run, no weather.json     Request 1                 Request 2 (temperature, wind)
Previous head                    wttr.in/?format=%l        wttr.in/Tel%20Aviv?format=%t|%w
Head                             wttr.in/?format=j1        wttr.in/Orient?format=%t|%w
```

In wttr.in's public source, a name in the URL path is geocoded as a bare string, and the geocoder's first result is used. The region, country and coordinates from the panel's `nearest_area` are not sent. A location-less request is resolved from the client IP instead, the same way as the panel's j1 request.

**Impact:** for a place name shared by several places, the notification can show the panel's place name with another place's temperature and wind. If the geocoder does not know the name, the notification says "Weather unavailable". The same script also backs the optional post-boot weather hook. What wttr.in returns for "Orient" was not observed, because wttr.in was not contacted.

**Suggested change:** in automatic mode, have `omarchy-weather-status` request `https://wttr.in/?format=%t|%w` with no location. Alternatively, read temperature and wind from the same j1 response as the name. `omarchy-weather-icon` already uses the name as a query only when `weather.json` exists and is non-empty (lines 8-12). If the script also stopped exiting early when the place name is empty (lines 7-10), a location-less request would keep the notification working when a j1 response lacks `nearest_area`. wttr.in's source does not guarantee that field, although the #12904 response had it. This can be done here or as a follow-up.

**Optional test improvement:** the commit removed the negative `locationProc`/`wttrLocation` assertions. A mutation check showed that restoring base's `%l` lookup as `wttrLocation || Model.reportLocationName(areaInfo, configuredLocation)` passes the new test. The previous test caught it. Keeping those two negative assertions next to the new wiring check would restore that coverage.

**Comment:** the header of `bin/omarchy-weather-location` (lines 10-11) still describes the no-argument output as "the IP-detected city".

**Related open PRs:** #9977, #12138 and #12155 each change the `${name%%,*}` line in `bin/omarchy-weather-location` that this commit removes. #12967 changes the same panel label for #12904 and keeps a `%l` fallback. #12952 edits the `locationProc` block this PR deletes. Whichever merges later will need its overlapping changes reconciled.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head, previous head and base weather scripts, panel, bar widget, manual and tests, plus wttr.in's public source. `weather-test.sh` was run in an isolated sandbox with Node on the head, previous head and base, with mutation checks, stubbed curl edge cases and a stubbed right-click status run. Related open PRs were compared by their diffs only. wttr.in was not contacted and no Quickshell UI was run, so live provider responses and rendered output were not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
